issues: Kei Cannon described last week as Lakeside's worst ever: covers fell by 16 (1.72%) week on week and spend per head fell by £0.56 (2.49%) to £21.86.
Sales were down £1,302.90 (5.61%) week on week and £11,111.98 (33.67%) below target; it was the last week before half term and Halloween.
Kei Cannon lowered the Lakeside weekly budget target from £32,000 to £25,000 to reflect lower trading.
Kei Cannon disputed incorrect delivery items using photo evidence and recovered £1,740, and moved the Deliveroo tag inside the restaurant to monitor arrival times.
Lakeside achieved a 4.39 rating with mostly five star reviews from Tuesday to Sunday, and one 1 star review about a scheduled delivery order issue.
Labour ran at 23%, and wage revenue was 23.25% excluding Kei Cannon's own salary hours.
Compliance was 96% because a pH level check was missed on Wednesday while head chef Rio was working alone.
Staffing: two new BOH staff have been hired and started; Satyaman is on holiday and Alina is currently working at M19.
Ziang Lin told Kei Cannon to remove authorised absence entries used for free labour from staff clock ins and make sure those hours are properly recorded in Kobas.

Ziang Lin asked Kei Cannon to increase his on site presence and return to core daily operations and shifts to remove the delivery and labour issues, and noted the assistant general manager training deadline of 31 October had not been met.
Ziang Lin plans to visit Lakeside over the bank holiday weekend and asked Kei Cannon to snapshot the dashboard metrics daily in the management chat.
Upcoming: Halloween, half term pickups, After Dark, Bonfire Night and live entertainment; Lakeside wants Christmas decorations up on 6 November, with set up scheduled between 6 and 10 November.
Areas for improvement: getting more reviews, helping BOH with their Mapal tasks so compliance is 100%, and being more organised.

Region: the team aligned on implementing and keeping the dry ice presentation standard for volcano rolls and sashimi across sites: dry ice is poured at the table in a circular shape for volcano rolls, and sashimi is served on crushed ice in a red vegan ramen bowl with bamboo leaves and daikon to reduce dry ice waste.
